newsitem.title: GERMANY: EU seed crush, exports down in 3rd quarter.
newsitem.headline: EU seed crush, exports down in 3rd quarter.

text.p: Declining oilseeds supply since June and high prices depressed European Union crush volumes and third country exports, the Oil World newsletter said.
The independent publication said joint crushings of soybeans, sunseed and rapeseed in July-Sept were 5.67 million tonnes versus 6.27 million in the same 1995 period.
Soybean crushings were off 10 percent and those of rapeseed 18 percent below the third quarter of 1995.
Oil output of the three fell to 1.61 million tonnes versus 1.78 million in third quarter 1995.

Meal output declines in Germany, Spain and Italy resulted in a reduced 3.91 million tonne meal total versus 4.91 million a year earlier. June, July and August export data from Britain, France and the Netherlands showed sharply reduced rape oil shipments abroad while German figures were unavailable.
Oil World said Chinese oil buyers had re-emerged in early October but it was hard to gauge the impact of their activity.
Current rape oil price premiums over soyoil in Europe had put off North African buyers, who had switched to alternatives such as soy and sun oil.
